title.narrative: Arab Reform Initiative: Climate Justice in MENA
Arab Reform Initiative: Climate Justice in MENA

description.narrative: Det föreslagna projektet "Strengthening Civil Society Actors and Networks Advocating for a Just Environmental Transition in the Middle East and North Africa" ??är ett program som bygger kapacitet hos civilsamhällesorganisationer att bli kompetenta och synliga aktörer i klimatdialogen i MENA-regionen. Sida-programmet är utformat för att vara helt integrerat i ett EU (DG NEAR) finansierat program med titeln "Strengthening Civil Society Actors: Toward a Just Environmental Transition in the Middle East and North Africa", som redan har fått finansiering för en 4-årsperiod med start från 1 januari 2023. Sida-medfinansieringen är planerad till en genomförandeperiod på 2,5 år med start 1 juni 2023 med en budget på 10 MSEK eller ~861 000 €, vilket motsvarar ~33% av programmets totala budget. Sida-medlen kommer att användas för att täcka EU-programmets 10-procentiga kostnadsandel för att specifikt stärka ungdoms- och feministiska CSO-nätverk, utöka aktiviteter till ytterligare länder, nämligen Algeriet, Jordanien, Irak, Palestina och Jemen, och för att stödja CSO:er att följa, övervaka och bidra till processrelaterade internationella klimatförhandlingar.

The intervention "Strengthening Civil Society Actors and Networks Advocating for a Just Environmental Transition in the Middle East and North Africa" aims at promoting capacities of CSOs to become competent and vocal actors in the climate action in the Mena region. The Sida co-financing is designed to be fully integrated into an EU (DG-NEAR) funded programme titled "Strengthening Civil Society Actors: Toward a Just Environmental Transition in the Middle East and North Africa". The Sida co-financing is scheduled for an implementation period for 2.5 years starting 1 June 2023 with a budget of 10 MSEK. The Sida funds will be utilised to cover the 10% cost share of the EU programme to specifically strengthen youth and feminist CSO networks, expand activities to additional countries namely, Algeria, Jordan, Iraq, Palestine and Yemen, and to support CSOs to follow, monitor and contribute to processes related international climate negotiations.

Next are examples of the expected results generated by the project:
1. The project contributed to improved understanding of the concept of just transitions among CSOs which is the main goal for the programming. During the Green Bridge project consultation meetings, CSOs had the chance to discuss ideas and learn from the experience of others. The project successfully engaged participants from various CSOs in 11 consultations across Egypt, Lebanon, Morocco, and Tunisia. These workshops and consultations focused on topics such as just environmental transition, energy policies, and local environmental challenges.
2. The project contributed to enhanced policy dialogues among the targeted stakeholders. The project produced four policy papers, covering topics like energy transition and environmental policies. Additionally, the project facilitated 11 meetings with key stakeholders, including EU delegations and local government officials. For example, ARI met with the EU delegation in Tunisia to discuss the role of the EU in promoting just environmental transition in Tunisia.
3. The project continues to push for regional cooperation and networking. A regional working group on energy was established focusing on developing insights and strategies for energy policy and just transition. The project also held an annual conference in Beirut, which brought together 60 in-person attendees and 300 online registrants to discuss topics such as environmental justice, energy transition, and climate finance. This conference served as a platform for regional cooperation and networking.
4. The project started working on dissemination and outreach. The project produced two webinars, and two podcast episodes. Additionally, five social media campaigns were launched, reaching 68,000 people, and nine videos were produced, garnering 31,145 unique views. For example, the webinar titled Just Environmental Transitions in Arab Politics provided a space for the exchange of ideas and perspectives among CSOs and experts.
5. The project featured youth participation within the climate justice discussion. The project held a capacity-building workshop for 32 youth organizations during the Climate Justice Camp in Lebanon. It also actively participated in COP28, focusing on youth voices and climate finance. Events and video interviews highlighted the work of MENA youth activists, such as the panel discussion on climate finance and just transition at the Swedish Pavilion during COP28, which featured youth speakers from Tunisia, Jordan, Lebanon, and Yemen.
